claims.text: The target domain is multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states near their melting temperatures.
Replacing EAM references with a machine-learned interatomic potential will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch in both solid and liquid states near melting.
The proposed machine-learned potential should be trained on a diverse set of ab initio configurations spanning high-temperature behaviors and atomic arrangements.
The method is applicable to alloys with at least five principal components near or above their melting points.
Atomic configurations in these high-temperature multicomponent alloys are highly diverse.
Existing EAM potentials exhibit phase-space mismatch in the stated regime.
A machine-learned potential can capture many-body interactions and the full spectrum of liquid atomic configurations.
Training on a comprehensive ab initio dataset allows the machine-learned potential to reproduce the energetic landscape more accurately than traditional EAM references.
The machine-learned potential reproduces local atomic environments more accurately than traditional EAM references.
More accurate energies and local environments lead to better sampling of configurational space.
Better configurational sampling produces a more continuous and less mismatched thermodynamic-integration path.
The machine-learned potential will significantly reduce thermodynamic-integration mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The potential reduction in thermodynamic-integration mismatch is 30–50%.
TOR-TILD's EAM references exhibit notable thermodynamic-integration path mismatch because they inadequately represent the many configurations of the ab initio liquid.
The anticipated improvement is primarily applicable to multicomponent systems near their melting temperatures.
Efficacy at lower temperatures or in less compositionally complex systems is uncertain.
The quantitative reduction in mismatch depends strongly on training-data quality, model architecture, and alloy composition.
A statistically significant failure to reduce free-energy path error relative to EAM under identical conditions would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The stated applicability is restricted to alloys with at least five principal components, but the proposed decisive test may use a binary alloy. Failure in a binary system would therefore fall outside the claimed domain and would not decisively falsify the stated high-entropy-alloy hypothesis.
